==English== {{swp|}} ===Alternative forms=== * {{q|obsolete}} {{l|en|waight}} ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/weɪt/}} * {{IPA|en|/weɪt/|[weɪ̯ʔt]|a=GA}} * {{audio|en|en-us-wait.ogg|a=US}} * {{audio|en|En-uk-to wait.ogg|a=UK}} * {{IPA|en|a=Indic|/wɛjʈ/|/weʈ/}} * {{rhymes|en|eɪt|s=1}} * {{homophones|en|weight}} ===Etymology 1=== {{root|en|ine-pro|*weǵ-}} From {{inh|en|enm|waiten}}, from {{der|en|xno|waiter}}, {{m|fro|waitier}} (compare {{cog|fr|guetter}} from {{cog|fro|gaitier}}, {{m|fro|guaitier}}), from {{der|en|frk|*wahtwēn|t=to watch, guard}}, derivative of {{der|en|frk|*wahtu|t=guard, watch}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*wahtwō|t=guard, watch}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*weǵ-|t=to be fresh, cheerful, awake}}. Cognate with {{cog|goh|wahtēn||to watch, guard}}, {{cog|nds-de|wachten||to wait}}, {{cog|nl|wachten||to wait, expect}}, {{cog|fr|guetter||to watch out for}}, {{cog|stq|wachtje||to wait}}, {{cog|fy|wachtsje|t=to wait}}, {{cog|frr|wachtjen||to stand, stay put}}. More at {{l|en|watch}}. In some senses, merged or influenced by {{der|en|enm|waiten}}, {{m|enm|weiten|t=to do good to, lie in wait for, to contrive good or harm on, catch, snare}}, from {{der|en|non|veita|t=to give help to, assist, grant, cause to happen}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*waitijaną|t=to show, guide, advise, direct}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*weyd-|t=to see, know}}. Largely overtook native {{ncog|enm|biden}}, from {{ncog|ang|bīdan}}, source of {{m|en|bide}}. ====Verb==== {{en-verb}} # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[delay]] [[movement]] or [[action]] until some event or time; to [[remain]] neglected or in readiness. #: {{ux|en|'''Wait''' here until your car arrives.}} #: {{ux|en|I’m still '''waiting''' for you to pay me back the money I lent you..}} #* {{RQ:Milton Poems 1673|When I Consider|page=59|pageref=n74|passage=They also serve who only stand and '''wait'''.}} #* {{RQ:Dryden Virgil|Aeneis |passage=Haste, my dear father; 'tis no time to '''wait'''.}} #* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|chapter=IV|page=46|passage=No matter how early I came down, I would find him on the veranda, smoking cigarettes, or otherwise his man would be there with a message to say that his master would shortly join me if I would kindly '''wait'''.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive|stative|US}} To [[wait tables]]; to serve customers in a [[restaurant]] or other [[eating]] [[establishment]]. #: {{ux|en|She used to '''wait''' in this joint.}} # {{lb|en|transitive|now|rare}} To delay movement or action until the arrival or occurrence of; to [[await]]. (Now generally superseded by “[[wait for]]”.) #: {{coi|en|to '''wait''' one’s turn}} #* {{RQ:Dryden Virgil|Aeneis |passage=Awed with these words, in camps they still abide, / And '''wait''' with longing looks their promised guide.}} #* {{RQ:Buchan Greenmantle|||“There is a dry wind blowing through the East, and the parched grasses '''wait''' the spark.”}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1992|author=w:Hilary Mantel|title=A Place of Greater Safety|publisher=Harper Perennial|year_published=2007|page=30 |passage=The Court had assembled, to '''wait''' events, in the huge antechamber known as the Œil de Boeuf.}} # {{lb|en|transitive|obsolete}} To [[attend]] on; to [[accompany]]; especially, to attend with ceremony or respect. #* {{RQ:Dryden Virgil|Aeneis |passage=He chose a thousand horse, the flower of all / His warlike troops, to '''wait''' the funeral.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1714|author=w:Nicholas Rowe|title=The Tragedy of Jane Shore |passage=Remorse and heaviness of heart shall '''wait''' thee, / And everlasting anguish be thy portion.}} # {{lb|en|obsolete}} To attend as a consequence; to [[follow]] upon; to [[accompany]]. # {{lb|en|obsolete|colloquial}} To [[defer]] or [[postpone]] (especially a meal). #* {{quote-book|en|year=1791|author={{w|Charlotte Smith (writer)|Charlotte Smith}}|title=Celestina|publisher=Broadview|year_published=2004|page=185 |passage=Montague Thorold, who impatiently watched her wherever she went, came to tell her that his mother '''waited''' breakfast for her.}} # {{lb|en|obsolete|except in phrases}} To watch with [[malicious]] intent; to [[lie in wait]] # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To remain [[faithful]] to one’s [[partner]] or [[betrothed]] during a [[prolonged]] period of absence. #* {{quote-book|en|year=1957|author=Dagny Taggart; Francisco d'Anconia, Ayn Rand's|title=[[w:Atlas_Shrugged|Atlas Shrugged]] |passage=She did not question him. Before leaving, she asked only, "When will I see you again?" He answered, "I don't know. Don't '''wait''' for me, Dagny. Next time we meet, you will not want to see me."}} #* {{quote-song|en|year=1974|author=w:The Bee Gees|title=w:Night Fever |passage=''I will '''wait''' / Even if it takes forever / I will wait / Even if it takes a lifetime''}} =====Usage notes===== * In sense 1, this is a [[catenative]] verb that takes the ''to infinitive''. See [[Appendix:English catenative verbs]] =====Conjugation===== {{en-conj|old=1}} =====Synonyms===== * {{sense|delay until}} {{l|en|await}}, {{l|en|wait for}}; See also [[Thesaurus:wait for]] *
